questions.question: Which of the following provides evidence that the Great Indian Desert was once under the sea during the Mesozoic era?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marine deposits and wood fossils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Great Indian Desert**, also known as the **Thar Desert**, has a geological history that reveals it was once submerged under the sea during the **Mesozoic era**, specifically during the **Jurassic** and **Cretaceous** periods.
 
• The presence of extensive **marine deposits** in the **Jaisalmer** and **Bikaner** regions serves as primary evidence of ancient **marine transgressions** where the **Tethys Sea** covered large parts of western **Rajasthan**.
 
• Evidence of this maritime past is preserved at the **Akal Wood Fossil Park**, located about 17 km from **Jaisalmer**, which contains petrified remains of **gymnosperms** and other trees dating back nearly **180 million years**.
 
• The discovery of fossilized **ammonites**, **bivalves**, and other marine invertebrates within the sedimentary rock layers confirms that the region supported a diverse marine ecosystem before tectonic shifts caused the sea to retreat.
 
• Geologists have identified that the desert floor consists of sedimentary rocks like **sandstones**, **limestones**, and **shales**, which are characteristic of shallow marine environments and coastal deltas from the **Mesozoic** and **Cenozoic** eras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other options do not serve as evidence for this specific geological phenomenon:
 
 
• **Black soil**:

 
 
• Also known as **Regur soil**, it is typically formed from the weathering of **basaltic** volcanic rocks.
 
• It is predominantly found in the **Deccan Trap** region, covering states like **Maharashtra** and **Madhya Pradesh**, rather than being an indicator of marine history in the **Thar**.
 
 
 
• **Glacial deposits**:
 
 
• These are sediments like **tillites** transported and deposited by glaciers.
 
• While found in the **Himalayas** or related to the **Permo-Carboniferous** glaciation of **Gondwanaland**, they are not the defining evidence for the **Mesozoic** sea in the **Thar**.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic ash layers**:
 
 
• These originate from explosive volcanic eruptions.
 
• While some volcanic activity occurred during the **Deccan** eruptions, they do not prove the existence of an ancient sea bed compared to the direct evidence of **fossilized marine life**.

questions.question: Which option is used in Windows 11 to temporarily turn off the computer to save power while keeping programs open?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hibernate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hibernate** is a power management mode in **Windows 11** designed to save the current state of the **Operating System**, including all open applications and documents, to the **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)** or **Solid State Drive (SSD)**.
 
• When this mode is activated, the system writes the contents of the **Random Access Memory (RAM)** into a hidden file located in the root directory of the system drive named **hiberfil.sys**.
 
• Unlike **Sleep mode**, which requires a small amount of power to keep data active in the volatile **RAM**, **Hibernate** uses **zero power** because the computer is physically powered down after the data transfer to storage is complete.
 
• It is particularly useful for **laptop users** who need to stop working for an extended period without a power source, as it ensures that the session is preserved even if the battery drains completely.
 
• When the user triggers a **Power On**, the **Windows Boot Loader** reads the data from the storage drive and restores it to the **RAM**, allowing the user to resume work exactly where they left off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shut Down**:

 
 
• This process closes all running programs, logs out the user, and clears the **RAM** entirely before cutting power to the hardware.
 
• In **Windows 11**, if **Fast Startup** is enabled, it saves a small part of the **Kernel** state to the disk to speed up the next boot process.
 
 
 
• **Restart**:
 
 
• This command initiates a full **Shut Down** followed by an immediate boot-up sequence.
 
• It is the standard procedure for clearing temporary software conflicts and finalizing the installation of **system updates** or **device drivers**.
 
 
 
• **Sleep**:
 
 
• Often confused with hibernation, this is a **low-power state** where data is kept in the **RAM** for near-instant wake times.
 
• If power is lost while in this mode, any unsaved data that was not previously backed up to the **Hard Drive** will be lost.

questions.question: Which continent has the highest average elevation due to its thick ice sheets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antarctica**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antarctica** is globally recognized as the highest continent in terms of **average elevation**, reaching approximately **2,300 meters** (roughly **7,500 feet**) above mean sea level.
 
• This distinction is not due to the height of its bedrock, but rather the presence of massive, permanent **ice sheets** that cover approximately **98%** of the landmass.
 
• The **Antarctic Ice Sheet** has an average thickness of about **1.9 kilometers** (**1.2 miles**), and in certain locations, the ice reaches depths of nearly **4.8 kilometers**.
 
• Without this thick layer of ice, **Antarctica** would likely be the lowest continent, as the weight of the ice causes **isostatic depression**, pushing much of the continental crust below sea level.
 
• In contrast, other continents consist primarily of exposed rock and soil, with their average elevations calculated based on their varied terrain of mountains, plateaus, and plains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asia**:

 
 
• While home to the world’s highest point, **Mount Everest** (**8,848.86 meters**), its vast plains and lowlands result in an average elevation of approximately **950 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Africa**:
 
 
• Characterized by extensive plateaus and the **East African Highlands**, its average elevation is roughly **600 meters**.
 
 
 
• **South America**:
 
 
• Despite containing the **Andes Mountains**, the longest continental mountain range, the continent maintains an average elevation of about **590 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Europe**:
 
 
• Considered the lowest continent by average elevation, standing at only **300 meters**, largely due to the massive **North European Plain**.

questions.question: Who among the following was a ruler of the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) dynasty of Kalinga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kharavela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kharavela** was the third and most illustrious ruler of the **Mahameghavahana dynasty**, also referred to as the **Chedi dynasty** of **Kalinga**.
 
• He reigned during the **1st or 2nd century BCE**, significantly expanding the power of **Kalinga** (modern-day **Odisha**) following the disintegration of the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
• The primary historical source for his reign is the **Hathigumpha inscription**, a seventeen-line record carved in the **Udayagiri Hills** near **Bhubaneswar**.
 
• The inscription provides a chronological account of his first thirteen years, mentioning his military victories over the **Satavahanas**, the **Indo-Greek** king **Demetrius**, and various **Tamil** kingdoms.
 
• A staunch follower of **Jainism**, Kharavela is credited with retrieving the **Kalinga Jina** idol from **Magadha** and constructing rock-cut caves for **Jain monks** at **Udayagiri** and **Khandagiri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni**:

 
 
• The 23rd ruler and the most powerful king of the **Satavahana dynasty**, who ruled the **Deccan** and **Central India**.
 
• He is celebrated in the **Nashik inscription** for destroying the **Saka**, **Yavana**, and **Pahlava** rulers and restoring the glory of the **Satavahanas**.
 
 
 
• **Kanishka**:
 
 
• The greatest emperor of the **Kushan dynasty**, who ruled over a vast territory spanning **Central Asia** and **North India**.
 
• He is famous for starting the **Saka Era** in **78 CE** and convening the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in **Kashmir** to resolve sectarian disputes.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga**:
 
 
• The founder of the **Shunga dynasty**, who ascended the throne in **185 BCE** after assassinating the last **Maurya** emperor, **Brihadratha**.
 
• He was a champion of **Brahmanical traditions** and performed two **Ashvamedha** (horse) sacrifices to assert his imperial authority.

questions.question: Which term describes sound energy received per second per unit area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intensity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound intensity** is scientifically defined as the amount of **sound energy** passing through a **unit area** per unit time (per second) in a direction perpendicular to that area.
 
• The relationship is mathematically expressed as **I = P / A**, where **I** is intensity, **P** is **sound power** (energy per second), and **A** is the **surface area**.
 
• Intensity is an **objective physical quantity** that can be accurately measured using instruments, regardless of the listener’s hearing sensitivity.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of sound intensity is **Watt per square meter** (W/m²).
 
• The intensity of sound is directly proportional to the **square of the amplitude** of the vibration. This means if the amplitude of the wave is tripled, the intensity increases by a factor of nine.
 
• While intensity is often associated with **loudness**, they are not the same; loudness is the subjective physiological response of the human ear to the intensity of sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency**

 
 
• It is the number of complete **oscillations** or cycles of a sound wave produced in one second.
 
• The unit of frequency is **Hertz** (Hz). It determines the **pitch** of the sound but is independent of the energy-per-area measurement.
 
 
 
• **Pitch**
 
 
• It is the **subjective perception** of the frequency of a sound by the human brain.
 
• Sounds with higher frequencies are perceived as **high-pitched** (shrill), while sounds with lower frequencies are perceived as **low-pitched** (flat).
 
 
 
• **Echo**
 
 
• An **echo** is the **reflection** of sound that reaches the listener shortly after the direct sound.
 
• To distinguish an echo from the original sound, the reflected sound must reach the ear at least **0.1 seconds** later, requiring a minimum distance of approximately **17.2 meters** in air at room temperature.

questions.question: Which heat transfer method enables the Sun to warm Earth, despite the vast empty space between them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radiation** is the unique method of heat transfer that does not require any **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate, allowing energy to travel through the **vacuum** of space.
 
• Energy from the Sun is transmitted in the form of **electromagnetic waves**, primarily consisting of **visible light**, **infrared radiation** (heat), and **ultraviolet rays**.
 
• Because the vast expanse between the Sun and the Earth is nearly a perfect **vacuum**, other methods like conduction or convection are impossible as they rely on **molecular interaction** or fluid movement.
 
• Thermal radiation travels at the **speed of light**, which is approximately **3 × 10⁸ meters per second**, ensuring that solar energy reaches Earth in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
 
• Once these electromagnetic waves strike the Earth's **atmosphere** and surface, the energy is absorbed by molecules, increasing their **kinetic energy** and resulting in a rise in **temperature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conduction**

 
 
• This is the transfer of heat through **direct contact** between substances.
 
• It occurs as faster-moving molecules collide with slower ones, passing **thermal energy** through a medium, typically effective in **solids** like metals.
 
 
 
• **Convection**
 
 
• It involves the **mass movement of molecules** within fluids, which includes both **liquids** and **gases**.
 
• Heated fluid becomes less dense and rises, while cooler, denser fluid sinks, creating **convection currents** that distribute heat.
 
 
 
• **Insulation**
 
 
• This is not a heat transfer method but rather the process of **reducing heat flow** between objects.
 
• **Thermal insulators** like fiberglass, wool, or trapped air are used to inhabit the transfer of energy via conduction or convection.

questions.question: The British gained control over Bengal after which major battle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** was fought on **June 23, 1757**, on the banks of the **Bhagirathi River** in Bengal.
 
• The conflict occurred between the **British East India Company**, commanded by **Robert Clive**, and the **Nawab of Bengal**, **Siraj-ud-Daulah**.
 
• A primary reason for the British victory was the secret alliance between **Robert Clive** and **Mir Jafar**, the commander of the Nawab’s army, who defected during the battle.
 
• The victory transformed the **British East India Company** from a commercial entity into a dominant political and military force in India, establishing its first major foothold in the wealthy province of **Bengal**.
 
• Following the battle, the British gained immense wealth from the Bengal treasury and were granted significant land and revenue rights, facilitating their subsequent expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Buxar (1764)**:

 
 
• This battle was fought between the British and the combined forces of **Mir Qasim** (Nawab of Bengal), **Shuja-ud-Daulah** (Nawab of Awadh), and the Mughal Emperor **Shah Alam II**.
 
• It consolidated British control over northern India and led to the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**, which granted the Company the **Diwani rights** to collect taxes from Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Wandiwash (1760)**:
 
 
• A decisive engagement during the **Third Carnatic War** between the British and the **French**.
 
• The British victory led by **Sir Eyre Coote** effectively ended French colonial ambitions in India.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Panipat**:
 
 
• The **Third Battle of Panipat (1761)** was fought between the **Maratha Empire** and the Afghan forces of **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.
 
• While it resulted in a Maratha defeat, it significantly weakened indigenous powers, indirectly aiding British ascendancy.

questions.question: The 20-Point Economic Programme was initially launched in 1975 primarily to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accelerate socio-economic reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Twenty Point Programme (TPP)** was first launched by Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** on **July 1, 1975**, with the primary objective of improving the quality of life of the **poor and underprivileged** sections of society.
 
• The programme was designed to facilitate growth with social justice by addressing critical areas such as **land reforms**, **liquidating rural indebtedness**, and ensuring the **abolition of bonded labor**.
 
• It focused on increasing **agricultural production**, implementing a **land ceiling**, and providing housing sites for the landless, which were essential components of the **socio-economic reform** agenda of that era.
 
• The initiative was closely linked to the **Fifth Five-Year Plan** and the slogan of **Garibi Hatao** (Eradicate Poverty), aiming to provide basic necessities like **clean drinking water**, **health**, and **education** to the rural masses.
 
• The programme sought to redistribute resources and curb **economic inequalities** by socializing urban land and preventing the hoarding of essential commodities. Hence, the primary aim was to accelerate socio-economic reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Evolution of TPP:
 
 
• The programme has been restructured multiple times in **1982**, **1986**, and most recently in **2006** (known as **TPP-2006**) to address contemporary challenges.
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring the implementation of the programme across various states.
 
 
 
• Distinction from Other Economic Shifts:
 
 
• **Liberalize trade policies** and **Promote foreign direct investment** were the core features of the **New Economic Policy** introduced in **1991**, commonly known as **LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** reforms.
 
• The 1975 programme was launched during the **Emergency** and focused on **domestic social welfare** rather than market-oriented liberalization or **reducing government borrowing**.

questions.question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts is used to copy selected text or objects?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + C** is the primary command used in **Graphical User Interfaces (GUI)** to duplicate **Selected Text**, **Images**, or **Files** without removing them from their original location.
 
• When this shortcut is executed, the operating system places a copy of the selected data into a temporary storage area known as the **Clipboard**, which resides in the **Random Access Memory (RAM)**.
 
• This command follows the **Common User Access (CUA)** standards, making it a universal shortcut across **Windows**, **Linux**, and various application softwares like **Microsoft Office** and **Web Browsers**.
 
• Unlike the **Cut** command, **Ctrl + C** is a non-destructive process that ensures the integrity of the source data while allowing for replication in another environment or document.
 
• In certain **Command-Line Interfaces (CLI)**, such as the **Linux Terminal**, the same key combination is often used to send a **SIGINT (Signal Interrupt)** to stop a running program, though its primary role in desktop computing remains copying.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ctrl + F**

 
 
• This shortcut activates the **Find** or **Search** utility, enabling users to locate specific keywords or character strings within a **Document**, **PDF**, or **Webpage**.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + S**
 
 
• Known as the **Save** command, this shortcut writes the current state of a file from the **Volatile Memory** to a **Permanent Storage Device** like an **SSD** or **HDD**.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + V**
 
 
• This is the **Paste** shortcut, which retrieves the content currently held in the **System Clipboard** and inserts it into the current cursor position or active window.

• A score of **67.0** indicates that India is approximately 67 percent of the way toward achieving the optimal target across the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, where a score of 100 represents full achievement.

questions.question: Which of the following provisions was brought about by the Indian Councils Act of 1909?

options.text: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims
Establishment of the Supreme Court in India
Universal voting rights for all Indians

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1909**, popularly known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, introduced the system of **separate electorates** based on religion. Under this provision, **Muslim** members were to be elected exclusively by **Muslim** voters, thereby institutionalizing communal representation in the Indian political system.
 
• This act effectively legalized **communalism** in **India**, and **Lord Minto** came to be known as the **Father of Communal Electorate** for his role in implementing this divisive electoral policy.
 
• The reform significantly increased the size of the **Legislative Councils** at both the **Central** and **Provincial** levels, where the number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from **16 to 60**.
 
• It empowered members of the **Legislative Council** to ask **supplementary questions** and move **resolutions** on the **Budget**, expanding the deliberative functions of the legislative bodies beyond mere discussion.
 
• The act provided for the first time for the association of **Indians** with the **Executive Councils** of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**, leading to the appointment of **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** as the first **Indian** member of the **Viceroy’s Executive Council**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context of Other Options:**

 
 
• The **Supreme Court in India** was first established at **Calcutta** through the **Regulating Act of 1773**, with **Sir Elijah Impey** as the first **Chief Justice**.
 
• **Universal voting rights** or **Universal Adult Franchise** was not granted during the **British Raj**; it was formally adopted only with the enforcement of the **Constitution of India** on **January 26, 1950**.
 
• The position of the **Viceroy** was created by the **Government of India Act 1858** following the **Revolt of 1857** and remained the supreme executive authority until the **Indian Independence Act of 1947**.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1919** (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) later introduced **Dyarchy** in the provinces and expanded the principle of communal representation to **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, and **Anglo-Indians**.

questions.question: The architectural style of the Jagannath Temple is primarily associated with which of the following traditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalinga style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jagannath Temple** in **Puri**, **Odisha**, is a monumental example of the **Kalinga style** of architecture, which is a specialized sub-branch of the broader **Nagara** (North Indian) tradition.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by three distinct types of temples: **Rekha Deula** (tall curvilinear tower), **Pidha Deula** (pyramidal roofed square porch), and **Khakhara Deula** (rectangular temple with a barrel-vaulted roof).
 
• The main sanctum of the Jagannath Temple is a **Rekha Deula**, while the assembly hall or porch, known as the **Jagamohana**, follows the **Pidha Deula** structure.
 
• Construction was initiated in the **12th century** by King **Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**, showcasing the pinnacle of Odishan stone masonry.
 
• The temple complex is enclosed by two massive concentric walls: the outer **Meghanada Pacheri** and the inner **Kurma Bheda**, which protect the sacred deities **Jagannath**, **Balabhadra**, and **Subhadra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian style**

 
 
• Origin: Developed primarily in **South India** under dynasties like the **Cholas** and **Pallavas**.
 
• Features: Characterized by a pyramid-like tower called a **Vimana** and massive gateways known as **Gopurams**.
 
 
 
• **Hoysala Style**
 
 
• Origin: Flourished in **Karnataka** between the 11th and 14th centuries.
 
• Features: Distinguished by a **stellate (star-shaped)** ground plan and extremely intricate carvings on **chloritic schist** (soapstone).
 
 
 
• **Vesara style**
 
 
• Origin: Emerged in the **Deccan** region, particularly under the **Later Chalukyas** and **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Features: A **hybrid style** that harmoniously combines elements of both the **Nagara** and **Dravidian** architectural traditions.

questions.question: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was established in which year?

• The **Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)** was established under the **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**, following the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The tribunal was officially inaugurated on **November 1, 1985**, during the tenure of the **Rajiv Gandhi** government to provide specialized adjudication for service-related disputes.
 
• The constitutional backing for the CAT is found in **Article 323-A**, which empowers the **Parliament** to establish administrative tribunals for the adjudication of disputes relating to recruitment and conditions of service.
 
• Its primary objective is to offer a **speedy** and **inexpensive** justice delivery mechanism to employees of the **Central Government**, thereby reducing the workload of the regular civil courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jurisdiction and Scope**:

 
 
• The **CAT** exercises original jurisdiction over service matters concerning members of the **All-India Services**, **Central Civil Services**, and civilian employees of the **Defense Services**.
 
• It does not have jurisdiction over members of the **Armed Forces**, officers and servants of the **Supreme Court**, and the secretarial staff of the **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework and Composition**:
 
 
• The tribunal is a **multi-member body** consisting of a **Chairman** and various **Members** (Judicial and Administrative), all of whom are appointed by the **President of India**.
 
• In its proceedings, the tribunal is not bound by the technicalities of the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, but is governed by the **Principles of Natural Justice**.
 
• Following the **L. Chandra Kumar Case (1997)**, the decisions of the CAT can be challenged before the **Division Bench** of the respective **High Court** through a writ petition.

questions.question: Electrical energy can be calculated using which of the following formulas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Energy = Power times Time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrical Energy** represents the total work done by an electric current in maintaining the flow of charge through a circuit for a given duration.
 
• **Electric Power (P)** is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in an electrical circuit. It is mathematically expressed as **Power = Energy / Time**.
 
• By rearranging the fundamental definition of power, **Electrical Energy (E)** can be calculated as the product of the power consumed and the time interval over which it is used: **Energy = Power × Time**.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, energy is measured in **Joules (J)**. One Joule is defined as the energy transferred when a power of one **Watt (W)** is applied for one **Second (s)**.
 
• This relationship is fundamental for calculating electricity bills, where the total energy consumption is determined by the wattage of appliances and their duration of operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power Components**:

 
 
• **Electric Power** itself is the product of **Voltage (V)** and **Current (I)**. Therefore, energy can also be expressed as **Energy = Voltage × Current × Time**.
 
• The unit of power is the **Watt**, named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Unit of Energy**:
 
 
• The **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)** is the standard unit for commercial electricity consumption, often referred to as a **Unit**.
 
• One **Kilowatt-hour** is equal to 1000 Watts used for one hour (3600 seconds), which equates to **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law and Energy**:
 
 
• According to **Ohm’s Law**, **Voltage = Current × Resistance**. Substituting this into the energy formula yields **Energy = I² × R × t**, known as **Joule’s Law of Heating**.
 
• This formula explains how electrical energy is converted into heat energy in resistors.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, the ________is a state’s de jure head.

• **Article 154** mandates that the executive power of the **State** shall be vested in the **Governor** and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him.

• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, with a standard term of **five years**.

• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the elected government and is appointed by the **Governor** under **Article 164**.

• The **Calcutta Session** of the **Indian National Congress** was a special session held in **September 1920**, presided over by **Lala Lajpat Rai**.

• The strategy also emphasized **economic self-reliance** through the **boycott of foreign cloth** and the proactive **adoption of Khadi** (hand-spun cloth) and the **Charkha** (spinning wheel) to revive the domestic textile industry.
 
• This session marked the transition of the **Congress** from a middle-class pressure group into a **mass movement** by integrating social, political, and economic boycotts.

• **Legislative Councils and Swarajists**:
 
 
• While the 1920 strategy demanded a total boycott, leaders like **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru** later formed the **Swaraj Party** in 1923 to contest elections and negotiate reforms from within the councils.
 
 
 
• **Ahimsa and Non-Violence**:
 
 
• Gandhi’s strategy was strictly based on **Non-Violence** (Ahimsa), making the establishment of **armed village guards** or any form of violent resistance fundamentally incompatible with his philosophy of **Satyagraha**.

questions.question: Which sector in India includes activities such as cotton textile production and iron and steel manufacturing?

• **Iron and steel manufacturing** is a foundational heavy industry within this sector, utilizing **iron ore** to produce steel, which serves as a vital input for various other industries like infrastructure and automobiles.

• **Quaternary sector**: A specialized component of the tertiary sector that involves **knowledge-based** services. Examples include **Information Technology (IT)**, **Research and Development (R&D)**, and **financial planning**.

• The **Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)** is a critical statistical measure used within the **education sector** to determine the number of students enrolled in school at different grade levels, such as **primary**, **secondary**, and **tertiary** education.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the number of students enrolled in a specific level of education, regardless of age, by the population of the official age group corresponding to that level, and then multiplying the result by **100**.
 
• The **GER** serves as an indicator of the **educational capacity** of a country and the extent of participation in the schooling system by the eligible population.
 
• A unique characteristic of this ratio is that it can exceed **100%**; this occurs when students who are older or younger than the official age group (due to late entry or grade repetition) are enrolled in that specific level.
 
• In the context of **Higher Education** in India, the **All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE)** is the primary report that tracks and publishes the **GER** data annually.

questions.solution:

• **Kudremukh** is a mountain range located in the **Chikmagalur** district of **Karnataka**, situated within the **Western Ghats**, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The name **Kudremukh** literally translates to **Horse-face** in the **Kannada** language, describing the unique shape of one of the highest peaks in the region.
 
• The region is world-renowned for housing one of the largest deposits of **Magnetite** iron ore in the world, which is a high-grade mineral known for its magnetic properties.

• For logistical efficiency, the ore was transported in the form of **slurry** through a **110 km** long pipeline to the **New Mangalore Port** for international export.

questions.question: The 11th Schedule of the Constitution of India lists:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29 subjects for Panchayats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th Schedule** was added to the **Constitution of India** by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1992**, which institutionalized the **Panchayati Raj** system.
 
• It contains a list of **29 subjects** or functional items over which the **Panchayats** have the power to plan and implement schemes for **economic development** and **social justice**.
 
• This schedule is linked directly to **Article 243-G** of the Constitution, which defines the powers, authority, and responsibilities of **Panchayats**.
 
• The subjects mentioned in the schedule include **Agriculture**, **Land Improvement**, **Minor Irrigation**, **Animal Husbandry**, **Fisheries**, **Social Forestry**, **Small-scale Industries**, **Rural Housing**, and **Drinking Water**.
 
• The inclusion of this schedule aimed to decentralize power and ensure the participation of the rural population in the democratic process at the **grassroots level**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **12th Schedule**:

 
 
• It was added by the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**.
 
• It contains **18 functional items** related to the powers and responsibilities of **Municipalities** (Urban Local Bodies) under **Article 243-W**.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**:
 
 
• It is part of the **7th Schedule** of the Constitution, which divides legislative powers between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• It contains subjects like **Education**, **Forests**, and **Marriage**, where both the **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** can make laws.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**:
 
 
• These are contained in **Part IV-A** and **Article 51A** of the Constitution.
 
• They were added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**; currently, there are **11 duties**.

questions.question: If you measure the amount of electric charge flowing in a circuit, which SI unit would you use to record the result?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coulomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Coulomb** (symbol: **C**) is the derived **SI unit** of **electric charge**, which measures the total quantity of electricity flowing through a circuit.
 
• By definition, one coulomb is equivalent to the amount of charge transferred by a constant current of **one ampere** in **one second**.
 
• The relationship between charge, current, and time is given by the formula **Q = I × t**, where **Q** represents charge in coulombs, **I** represents current in amperes, and **t** represents time in seconds.
 
• Scientifically, a single coulomb is a large unit representing approximately 6.242 times 10¹⁸ **elementary charges** (electrons or protons).
 
• The unit is named after **Charles-Augustin de Coulomb**, the scientist who discovered **Coulomb’s Law**, which quantifies the electrostatic force between two point charges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volt**

 
 
• The **Volt** (V) is the SI unit for **electric potential**, potential difference, and **electromotive force** (EMF).
 
• It measures the energy available to move a unit charge; specifically, one volt is defined as **one joule per coulomb**.
 
 
 
• **Ampere**
 
 
• The **Ampere** (A) is the SI base unit for **electric current**.
 
• It represents the **rate** of flow of charge, where one ampere equals **one coulomb per second**.
 
 
 
• **Ohm**
 
 
• The **Ohm** (Ω) is the SI unit for **electrical resistance**.
 
• Based on **Ohm’s Law**, one ohm is the resistance of a conductor in which a potential difference of **one volt** produces a current of **one ampere**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional landform formed by wind action?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barchan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Barchan** is a **crescent-shaped** sand dune that is primarily formed by the **depositional action** of **wind**, a process known as **Aeolian action**.
 
• These landforms typically develop in arid regions where the **wind direction** remains relatively constant and there is a **limited supply of sand**.
 
• The **convex side** of a Barchan faces the prevailing wind (the **windward side**), while the **leeward side** forms a steep **slip face** between two projecting **horns**.
 
• The **horns** of the Barchan always point in the **downwind direction**, signifying the direction toward which the dune is slowly **migrating**.
 
• Barchans can range in height from a few meters to over **30 meters**, and their width between horns can reach several hundred meters depending on sand availability and **wind velocity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yardang**:

 
 
• It is an **erosional landform** carved by the **abrasive action** of wind-blown sand.
 
• It consists of streamlined, **elongated ridges** of resistant rock separated by grooves of softer material.
 
 
 
• **Inselberg**:
 
 
• An **isolated hill** or mountain that rises abruptly from a flat plain, often found in **desert landscapes**.
 
• It is an **erosional feature** created by the long-term **weathering** and removal of surrounding weaker rock layers.
 
 
 
• **Moraine**:
 
 
• This is a **depositional landform**, but it is formed by **glacial action** rather than wind.
 
• It consists of **unconsolidated debris** such as **glacial till**, boulders, and silt deposited by a moving or melting **glacier**.

questions.question: Where was the annual World Economic Forum meeting held in January 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Economic Forum (WEF)** organized its **55th Annual Meeting** in the alpine resort of **Davos-Klosters, Switzerland**, from **January 20 to 24, 2025**.
 
• The **2025 meeting** focused on the overarching theme of **Collaboration for the Intelligent Age**, reflecting the global shift toward **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and advanced computing.
 
• This gathering served as a platform for over **2,500 leaders** from the private sector, government, and international organizations to discuss the ethical, economic, and social implications of rapid **technological transformation**.
 
• Key agenda items included navigating the **global energy transition**, addressing **geopolitical fragmentation**, and fostering **sustainable economic growth** in a post-globalization landscape.
 
• The selection of **Davos** continues a decades-long tradition where the secluded mountain environment encourages informal yet high-stakes **diplomatic dialogue** and strategic partnerships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):**

 
 
• Founded in **1971** by **Klaus Schwab**, the **WEF** is an independent international organization committed to improving the state of the world through **public-private cooperation**.
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Cologny, Geneva, Switzerland**, and is officially recognized by the **Swiss Confederation** as an international body.
 
• It is renowned for championing **Stakeholder Capitalism**, a concept emphasizing that corporations should serve the interests of all society, not just their shareholders.
 
 
 
• **Davos-Klosters as a Venue:**
 
 
• Located in the **Graubünden** region of the **Swiss Alps**, it is the highest town in **Europe**, which provides the necessary security infrastructure for world leaders.
 
• The **Davos Manifesto**, originally drafted in **1973** and updated in **2020**, sets the ethical guidelines for the forum's interactions and its mission of global governance.
